toegepas.voor: So hoef 'n mens die pad minder kere heen en weer te stap
toegepas.na: So moes 'n mens die pad minder kere heen en weer stap
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Hoef' normally needs a negative, and the present tense breaks the block's past narrative ('kon'); 'moes' fixes both and saves a word.
toegepas.fout: 'hoef' stands without a negative ('minder kere hoef ... te stap'), which a careful editor marks as unnatural, and it repeats 'hoef' in the next-but-one sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'moes ... minder kere stap' is the natural form, says the same thing (fewer trips needed), echoes the opening block's 'moes die pad baie keer heen en weer stap', and saves a word.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Countable 'woud' without an article reads unnaturally; the plural is idiomatic and adds no words.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'deur digte woud' is normal Afrikaans with 'woud' used as a mass noun, so the plural is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Op sy rug of agter hom aan
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: op sy rug. Of hy trek
laat_vaar_vorige.na: op sy rug, of hy trek
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A sentence opening with 'Of' reads as a fragment; joining the two clauses with a comma before 'of' follows AWS and flows better.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The two short sentences set out the 'twee maniere' clearly for Grade 4, and joining them puts two 'of's in one sentence, which is harder to read.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: wat daar kan leef en werk
laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat daar kon leef en werk
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The sentence is in the past (het ... gekies), so the relative clause should be past too.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'wat daar kan leef en werk' is a general truth in the present, like 'Perde stap vinniger' that follows, so the swap is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Die plaas' points to one specific farm that was never introduced; the general statement needs 'plase'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Op die plaas' is idiomatic generic Afrikaans for farm life, so 'Op plase' is only a different wording.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: om vinniger te reis as wat 'n dier stap
laat_vaar_vorige.na: om vinniger te reis as wat 'n dier kon stap
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The comparison clause needs a modal in the past to match the past-tense sentence; 'as wat 'n dier stap' reads incomplete.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'as wat 'n dier stap' is a complete, natural general comparison, and the change only adds a word under a hard ceiling.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: net so vinnig gegaan as wat die dier kon gaan
laat_vaar_vorige.na: net so vinnig gegaan as wat die dier kon stap
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Avoids the clumsy repetition gegaan/gaan and matches 'stap' used for the animals throughout the lesson.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'kon stap' narrows the meaning to walking, while 'kon gaan' covers every pace an animal such as a horse can go, so the meaning would move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'na hom kyk' can read as 'look at him' (from English 'look after'); 'na hom omsien' clearly means care for him.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'na iemand kyk' is standard Afrikaans for looking after someone and is plainer for Grade 4 than the more formal 'omsien'.
